_readme: Golden vectors for the native-vs-docker build predicate.
TWO harnesses consume this ONE file and must agree:
bash: bin/build/test-strategy-parity.sh   (sources bin/build/strategy.sh)
rust: src/util/firestream-ci/src/platform/parity.rs (Probe fixtures)
A `case` is:
probe            filesystem/PATH conditions, injected by both harnesses
uname_s          value of `uname -s`
uname_m          value of `uname -m` (RAW, pre-normalisation)
nix_on_path      whether `nix` resolves on PATH
nix_store_present whether /nix/store is a directory
dockerenv_file   whether /.dockerenv exists
cgroup           contents of /proc/1/cgroup, or null when absent
target_arch      argument to fs_native_blocker/fs_choose_strategy; "" = default to host
env              process env (FIRESTREAM_BUILD_STRATEGY + container-route vars)
profile_default  ci-manifest.json build_strategy.default; RUST ONLY (shell is profile-blind)
expect.blocker   fs_native_blocker output; null = empty (native possible). ENV-INDEPENDENT.
expect.strategy  fs_choose_strategy output: native | docker
expect_shell     OPTIONAL. Only legal when profile_default is set and != "auto".
Records the shell's profile-blind answer. The bash harness
REFUSES any expect_shell outside that rule, so it cannot be
used to paper over real drift.
_arch_cases_note: input is never empty: get_nix_volume/fs_docker_platform use ${1:-$(uname -m)}, so an empty argument means 'the host arch', not 'the empty arch'. The empty-target semantics of the predicate are covered by the case named native-happy-path-empty-target-defaults-to-host.

cases.name: native-happy-path
cases.why: Linux, same arch, nix + /nix/store, not containerised.

cases.name: native-happy-path-empty-target-defaults-to-host
cases.why: Empty target_arch falls back to uname -m via ${1:-$(uname -m)}.

cases.name: native-happy-path-target-alias-normalises
cases.why: target amd64 normalises to x86_64 and matches an x86_64 host.

cases.name: native-happy-path-host-alias-normalises
cases.why: A host reporting amd64 still matches an x86_64 target.

cases.name: native-happy-path-unknown-arch-passthrough
cases.why: fs_norm_arch passes unknown arches through unchanged; equal is equal.

cases.name: blocker-1-non-linux-darwin
cases.why: Probe order slot 1. Image derivations are gated behind isLinux.

expect.blocker: host is not Linux (uname -s = Darwin); image derivations are gated behind isLinux

cases.name: blocker-1-non-linux-freebsd-interpolates-uname
cases.why: The uname -s value is interpolated verbatim, not hardcoded to Darwin.

expect.blocker: host is not Linux (uname -s = FreeBSD); image derivations are gated behind isLinux

cases.name: blocker-2-cross-arch
cases.why: Probe order slot 2. Both arches appear NORMALISED in the message.

expect.blocker: cross-arch target (aarch64) differs from host arch (x86_64)

cases.name: blocker-2-cross-arch-aliases-normalised-in-message
cases.why: target arm64 / host amd64 are reported as aarch64 / x86_64.

expect.blocker: cross-arch target (aarch64) differs from host arch (x86_64)

cases.name: blocker-2-cross-arch-unknown-target
cases.why: Unknown arches pass through normalisation and still compare unequal.

expect.blocker: cross-arch target (s390x) differs from host arch (x86_64)

cases.name: blocker-3-no-nix-on-path
cases.why: Probe order slot 3.

cases.name: blocker-4-no-nix-store
cases.why: Probe order slot 4. nix on PATH but no store (e.g. a stray wrapper).

expect.blocker: /nix/store does not exist on this host

cases.name: blocker-5-container-route-dockerenv
cases.why: fs_in_container route 1: /.dockerenv exists.

cases.name: blocker-5-container-route-kubernetes-service-host
cases.why: fs_in_container route 2: $KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST non-empty.

cases.name: blocker-5-container-route-CONTAINER-upper
cases.why: fs_in_container route 3: $CONTAINER non-empty.

cases.name: blocker-5-container-route-container-lower
cases.why: fs_in_container route 4: $container non-empty (systemd-nspawn/podman convention).

cases.name: blocker-5-container-route-cgroup-docker
cases.why: fs_in_container route 5a: /proc/1/cgroup matches 'docker'.

cases.name: blocker-5-container-route-cgroup-kubepods
cases.why: fs_in_container route 5b: /proc/1/cgroup matches 'kubepods'.

cases.name: blocker-5-container-route-cgroup-containerd
cases.why: fs_in_container route 5c: /proc/1/cgroup matches 'containerd'.

cases.name: not-a-container-cgroup-present-but-no-match
cases.why: Negative control for route 5: a cgroup file that matches none of the patterns.

cases.name: not-a-container-empty-container-env-vars
cases.why: Negative control: EMPTY (not unset) CONTAINER/container must not trip -n.

cases.name: order-linux-check-precedes-everything
cases.why: Every blocker applies at once; slot 1 must win.

expect.blocker: host is not Linux (uname -s = Darwin); image derivations are gated behind isLinux

cases.name: order-cross-arch-precedes-nix-store-container
cases.why: Slots 2..5 all apply; slot 2 must win.

expect.blocker: cross-arch target (aarch64) differs from host arch (x86_64)

cases.name: order-no-nix-precedes-no-store-and-container
cases.why: Slots 3..5 all apply; slot 3 must win.

cases.name: order-no-store-precedes-container
cases.why: Slots 4..5 both apply; slot 4 must win.

expect.blocker: /nix/store does not exist on this host

cases.name: env-force-native-on-clean-host
cases.why: FIRESTREAM_BUILD_STRATEGY=native is honoured; blocker is unaffected.

cases.name: env-force-native-overrides-a-real-blocker
cases.why: PRECEDENCE: the env var is read before any probing, so a Darwin host with no nix still reports native. This is the deliberate escape hatch; fs_native_blocker still reports the truth.

expect.blocker: host is not Linux (uname -s = Darwin); image derivations are gated behind isLinux

cases.name: env-force-docker-on-clean-native-host
cases.why: PRECEDENCE: total rollback with no code revert on a host that could build natively.

cases.name: env-auto-explicit-falls-through-to-probing
cases.why: auto is the documented no-op value.

cases.name: env-empty-string-is-auto
cases.why: ${FIRESTREAM_BUILD_STRATEGY:-auto} plus the explicit "" arm both mean auto.

cases.name: env-garbage-warns-and-is-treated-as-auto
cases.why: Unrecognised values must NOT fail closed to docker; they warn and probe.

cases.name: env-garbage-treated-as-auto-on-blocked-host
cases.why: Same, but probing then yields docker for a real reason.

cases.name: profile-default-docker-forces-on-clean-native-host
cases.why: PRECEDENCE: ci-manifest.json build_strategy.default sits BELOW FIRESTREAM_BUILD_STRATEGY and ABOVE probing. The shell is profile-blind and stays native.

cases.name: profile-default-native-forces-past-a-blocker
cases.why: PRECEDENCE: a profile that pins native behaves like the env var, one rung down.

cases.name: env-beats-profile-default
cases.why: PRECEDENCE: env native wins over profile docker. Both harnesses agree here because the env var alone determines the answer.

cases.name: env-docker-beats-profile-native
cases.why: PRECEDENCE: mirror of the above.

cases.name: profile-default-auto-is-a-no-op
cases.why: The schema default. Equivalent to the profile-blind shell, so no expect_shell.

cases.name: profile-default-garbage-warns-and-is-auto
cases.why: A malformed profile must not wedge the build; warn and probe.

expect.blocker: /nix/store does not exist on this host

expect_shell.blocker: /nix/store does not exist on this host

cases.name: env-garbage-then-profile-docker
cases.why: PRECEDENCE: an unrecognised env value degrades to auto, which then lets the profile speak.
